title: [Finding] 389238 Production, washing machine, V-ZUG (CH): the 2026 year-to-hour relabel leaves an annual inventory unscaled (×8,760 per unit)
body:
### BAFU activity code(s), name, geography, unit

389238 Production, washing machine, V-ZUG (CH, hr; `a` in BAFU:2025 v2)

### Release observed in

BAFU:2026 v1

### Where you looked

ecoSpold XML, `process_67a9453e-aca5-304a-83b0-f9e4bef2c44a.xml` (2026 v1 and 2025 v2), and all 11,947 (2026 v1) and 11,747 (2025 v2) files for consumers and for the rest of the group; the 2026 v1 datasets change log, sheet *Updated datasets*; the LCIA results workbooks 2025 and 2026 v1; the 2026 v1 and v1.1 database packages.

### What you measured, and how

```text
389238 is an aggregated dataset: type=2 in the XML, "LCI result" in the database package.
It has no technosphere inputs: 253 resource rows, 1,400 emission rows, 1 reference row.

                      2025 v2     2026 v1
reference unit        a           hr        (workbook: y -> h; package: h)
reference amount      1.0         1.0
exchange rows         1,654       1,654

Matched the rows of the two files on exchange number, location, unit and amount, as multisets:
1,653 of 1,654 are identical. The one that differs is the reference row itself (a -> hr).
With the unit label ignored, all 1,654 are identical. (Six `Water` rows to water, unspecified,
share one flow and compartment. Keyed on flow and compartment, it is 1,648 of 1,649.)

Amounts per reference unit, the same strings in both files:
  Carbon dioxide, fossil, to air (4 sub-compartments)    3,160,355 kg
  Carbon dioxide, in air                                   258,291.82 kg
  Methane, fossil, to air                                   11,659.95 kg
  Gas, natural/m3, in ground                             1,098,817.8 m3
  Gravel, in ground                                        309,111.8 kg
  Coal, brown, in ground                                   282,445.3 kg
  Coal, hard, in ground                                    167,910.8 kg
  Oil, crude, in ground                                     93,329.2 kg
Workbook GWP100: 3,579,489 kg CO2-eq per y (2025), 3,597,212 kg CO2-eq per h (2026 v1).
v1.1 database package: reference unit h, all 1,654 amounts identical to v1.

Change log: 389238 is listed under "Year unit correction", update type Corrected.
All 156 rows of that category match one dataset each by name and geography, with the same
number in both releases:
   87  reference unit a -> hr; every other amount unchanged
   69  reference unit kept (41 m3, 24 kg, 4 km); 259 input rows relabelled a -> hr,
       amounts unchanged
155 of the 156 are unit processes (type=1). 389238 is the only aggregated one.
The other 86 that moved to hr are hours of use: forestry machines 14, helicopters 10,
laser machining 14, computer, network, printer and home-office use 48. Their amounts are
of hourly scale, for example:
   525719 power sawing (RER)               1.6 kg two-stroke petrol per hr
   324673 passenger helicopter, twin-engine 259.3 kg kerosene, 816.79 kg fossil CO2 per hr
   284491 desktop computer, CRT, active      0.15 kWh per hr
The largest fossil CO2 to air among the 86 is that 816.79 kg. 389238 carries 3,869 times as much.
No dataset in 2026 v1 keeps the reference unit a. In 2025 v2, 87 did, and all 87 are now hr.
```

### Why it cannot be right

Only the label changed. In 2025 v2 the same amounts were per year. Read per hour, the dataset emits 3,160 t of fossil CO2 every hour, including its supply chain. That is 27.7 Mt a year for one manufacturer's washing-machine production. Read per year, as in 2025, it is 361 kg an hour on average, the scale of a factory and its supply chain.

The change log describes the category as fixing datasets that used the year where the hour was meant. For the 86 hour-of-use datasets the amounts fit an hour, so the new label is right for them. 389238 is not an hour of use: it is an aggregated result without technosphere inputs, and its amounts fit a year. Every reference unit `a` in the release became `hr`, so the correction seems to have caught this dataset too. That last part is our reading; the files do not say.

### Exposure, if known

No consumers: no exchange in 2026 v1 (or 2025 v2) buys 389238, so no other dataset's result moves. The exposure is direct use of the dataset or of its workbook row (3,597,212 kg CO2-eq per h): per hour, both are 8,760 times too high. Unchanged in the v1.1 database package.

### Suggested correction (optional)

Restore the reference unit `a` (year) on 389238 in the files, the database package and the workbook; the amounts are already per year. If a per-hour dataset is intended instead, divide all 1,653 other amounts by 8,760.

This is F27 in lci-bafu-catalog's ledger; the two ledgers share the number. Thread: [lci-bafu-catalog#44](https://gitlab.com/eos-lci/lci-bafu-catalog/-/issues/44).

Agent-run change.
